@graph.name: pba_synthesis
@graph.description: Synthesis of Prussian blue analogues (PBA) by co-precipitation in the K1 Start annular flow reactor of Lab 208 (Accelerated Materials). Solution A (potassium ferrocyanide) and solution B (nickel(II) chloride, in experiment 2 mixed with manganese(II) nitrate) are poured from stock solutions made up beforehand into two 500 mL bottles and pumped into the coaxial capillaries of the reactor, with compressed air as the core gas; the PBA precipitates from the ions in the mixing zone and is collected as a suspension in a beaker. Experiment 1: nickel; experiment 2: nickel and manganese. Planned by Meng Kong, performed by Chuyue Li.

Preparation
@graph.schema:description: Everything done before the main operation starts: charging, setting up, closing the apparatus.

@graph.schema:name: Work-up
@graph.schema:description: Everything done after the main operation: sampling, emptying, separating, washing, concentrating, purifying, analysing.

@graph.schema:name: Assuming the manganese(II) concentration
@graph.schema:description: The concentration of the manganese(II) nitrate solution is not recorded. It is taken as that of the nickel(II) chloride solution, 0.01 M, for the 1:1 ratio of the two metals - and so 0.005 M in bottle no. 2 of experiment 2, where the two solutions were mixed 1:1 by volume.

@graph.schema:name: Entering the run parameters
@graph.schema:description: Entered into the K1 control software before the start: reaction ID (ferro+ni, ferro+ni2+mn2), operator cl2114, reagent names (ferro; ni2+, ni2+mn2), the flow rates of pumps A and B (3 mL/min each - the log says L/min; mL/min confirmed by Meng Kong, 2026-10-08) and the reaction time of 120 s.

@graph.schema:name: Logging the run
@graph.schema:description: The K1 control software logs the run every 2.4 s - air mass flow rate and air temperature at the mass flow controller, the pump set points and pressures; it saves the log when the run stops; the log of experiment 2 holds both of its runs, one after the other. The pressure of pump B reads 0.0 throughout - perhaps only its baseline, why is not known (Meng Kong, 2026-10-08) - and is not taken.

@graph.schema:name: Filling the feed bottles
@graph.schema:description: The first task of each experiment - the ferrocyanide stock solution poured into bottle no. 1, the nickel(II) chloride stock solution into bottle no. 2; in experiment 2 the manganese(II) nitrate stock solution as well, mixed with the nickel one in bottle no. 2 - the two in equal volumes, just enough for one run (Meng Kong, 2026-10-14). It takes around 10 to 20 minutes (Meng Kong, 2026-10-08).

@graph.schema:name: Running the K1 reactor
@graph.schema:description: The two solutions are pumped into the reactor with the air core; the PBA precipitates in the mixing zone and the suspension runs into the beaker.

@graph.schema:name: Screwing on the caps
@graph.schema:description: After filling, the caps with their two ports screwed onto the feed bottles - the suction tube led through one port, the other left open. Until then the bottles stand open.

@graph.schema:name: Opening the air valve
@graph.schema:description: The first thing of an experiment - the valve of the compressed air line opened; it stays open the whole experiment, the reactor controls the mass flow controller.

@graph.schema:name: Priming the K1 system
@graph.schema:description: The tubes put into a beaker of water and the priming programme of the reactor run, before the reaction run; its order relative to filling the feed bottles does not matter. Always three minutes (Meng Kong, 2026-10-08).

@graph.schema:name: Taking a sample
@graph.schema:description: Near the end of the run a falcon tube held under the outlet tip instead of the beaker; how long follows from the flow rate and the volume wanted, which is read off the graduation of the tube.

@graph.schema:name: Extracting the run table
@graph.schema:description: The table of each run log written alone, with its header in the first row (generator/interfaces/instruments/k1_start_run_tables.py); the log of experiment 2 holds two runs - one table per run (Laura Fadler and Meng Kong, 2026-10-08).

@graph.schema:name: Rinsing the K1 system
@graph.schema:description: After the run, like priming, with water (after experiment 1) or dilute sulfuric acid (after experiment 2, the last of the day); repeated while the pressure stays higher than normal - one rinse each, as long as priming - three minutes (Meng Kong, 2026-10-08).

Assuming the times of the experiments
@graph.schema:description: Only the runs themselves are logged. Filling the feed bottles takes 10 to 20 minutes, priming and rinsing three minutes each (Meng Kong, 08.10.2026). Experiment 1 is taken to start 23 minutes before its run (14:02:25) - filling at most 20 minutes, then priming - and at the latest 13 minutes before it (filling at least 10 minutes). The first run of experiment 2 is not dated (it ended before the second began, 15:06:21); experiment 2 is taken to start right after experiment 1, whose run ended at 14:27:25 and whose rinse took three minutes (14:30:25). No end of the experiments is assumed. The tasks between are placed no earlier than the start of their experiment, priming at the latest three minutes before the (first) run, rinsing and emptying no earlier than the end of the (last) run.

Assuming the times of the experiments
@graph.schema:description: Only the runs themselves are logged. Filling the feed bottles takes 10 to 20 minutes, priming and rinsing three minutes each (Meng Kong, 08.10.2026). Experiment 1 is taken to start 23 minutes before its run (14:02:25) - filling at most 20 minutes, then priming - and at the latest 13 minutes before it (filling at least 10 minutes). The first run of experiment 2 is not dated (it ended before the second began, 15:06:21); experiment 2 is taken to start right after experiment 1, whose run ended at 14:27:25 and whose rinse took three minutes (14:30:25). No end of the experiments is assumed. The tasks between are placed no earlier than the start of their experiment, priming at the latest three minutes before the (first) run, rinsing and emptying no earlier than the end of the (last) run.
